caption: Does David’s everlasting throne predict Jesus’s eternal kingdom? The wider Christian reading is plausible, but the temple-building son first points to Solomon.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did David’s throne predict Jesus? God promises that David’s son will have an enduring throne. Second Peter calls Jesus’s kingdom eternal.
slides.body: God promises that David’s son will have an enduring throne. Second Peter calls Jesus’s kingdom eternal.
slides.heading: Did David’s throne predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of 2Sam 7:13: I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
slides.body: I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
slides.heading: 2Sam 7:13

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in 2 Pet 1:11, BSB: and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
slides.body: and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · 2 Pet 1:11

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians see Jesus here The old monarchy ended, but the promise remained. Christians see Jesus as David’s final heir whose kingdom truly lasts.
slides.body: The old monarchy ended, but the promise remained. Christians see Jesus as David’s final heir whose kingdom truly lasts.
slides.heading: Why Christians see Jesus here

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the first heir is Solomon This son builds the temple, which Solomon does. The verse promises an enduring Davidic throne but does not name its final king.
slides.body: This son builds the temple, which Solomon does. The verse promises an enduring Davidic throne but does not name its final king.
slides.heading: But the first heir is Solomon

title: The everlasting Davidic throne
